Adds assertNoUnauthorizedV1CorrelationV0(request) at every path through the shared runner/provider boundary (withQuotaObservation's run, resolveRunnerForModel's run, runImplementationForModel) — the provider/runner backstop plan §1.3 calls for. With LEGACY_UNCORRELATED_RUNNER_INVOCATION_REJECTED_V0 enabled, this now rejects legacy uncorrelated invocations too, not only unauthorized V1-correlated ones. Runner V1 cohort (plan §3.3/§3.4, executable-order step 5, closing the implementation review's selection/invocation-split blocker): adds openV1RunnerSelection, the registry's V1 reservation-based selection — it reuses the exact legacy ranking policy (resolveEffectiveProvider for the stored primary, backupModelsForStage for strategy-gated fallbacks), rejects mode-incapable candidates at selection time (preflight/edit and last-message-file CLIs return providerModeUnavailable), issues every reservation through the caller's ProviderSelectionSessionV1, and never invokes a provider itself — the registry remains the sole ranking/fallback authority while invocation moves to the execution broker. Step-5 CLI-cutover round (closing the implementation review's silent-bypass completion blocker): a ranked candidate that cannot satisfy the requested mode is no longer silently filtered out of the candidate list — when no ranked candidate supports the mode the whole selection returns providerModeUnavailable, and when a mode-incapable candidate (the primary or a mid-list backup) precedes a capable one, reserveNext settles the caller's attempt as an explicit providerUnavailablePreInvocation outcome and returns the new candidateUnavailable result naming the skipped candidate, so the unavailable primary is represented as a settled, auditable attempt before any backup attempt is allocated. The legacy resolveRunnerForModel/runImplementationForModel cascades still invoke fallback internally, but only for legacy routes that remain fail-closed behind the §1.3 gates until their cohorts migrate. Foundations round (plan §3.8, closing the implementation review's coordinator-boundary architectural blocker): adds createV1RunnerSelectionOpener, the production RunnerSelectionOpenerV1 for the action coordinator — it binds openV1RunnerSelection to the invocation-fixed workspace cwd and the invoking route's stage-model resolution, so the coordinator consumes this registry's operation-bound reserveNext contract verbatim (the registry ranks and reserves through the coordinator's session; the coordinator never selects a candidate or issues a reservation itself, and invocation stays with the execution broker).

annotations.rationale: Fixes a PID-reuse hazard in killProcessTree's Windows taskkill retry schedule: retries used to keep firing `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` against a fixed PID at delays up to 30s with no regard for whether the tracked child had already exited, so a stale retry could force-kill an unrelated process that Windows had assigned the reused PID in the meantime (observed as the intermittent `pnpm run test` red flagged by the implementation review: the cancellation-guard test's freshly spawned npm check was killed by a sibling test's stale retry — non-zero exit, empty output, no "[check cancelled]" marker). Each retry now no-ops once child.exitCode/signalCode is set, all pending retry timers are cleared on the child's 'exit' event, and the timers are unref'd so a pending retry never holds the process open. Once the spawned root has exited a retry could only ever hit a reused PID or fail — `/T` scopes the tree walk to that root, so it could never reach a surviving orphaned descendant anyway. killProcessTree is now exported @internal for the regression test (src/test/completionLintKillPidReuse.test.ts). The doc comment additionally records — per the implementation review's non-blocking suggestion — that the two guards are deliberately redundant and must BOTH survive any refactor. A follow-up review round noted the end-to-end regression test alone passes with either guard present, so per that round's non-blocking suggestion the function now accepts an @internal optional KillProcessTreeGuardSeam parameter (omitFireTimeExitCheck / omitExitTimeTimerCleanup) that disables exactly one guard at a time; two Windows-only seam tests in the same test file each disable one guard and fail if the other has been removed, making both guards independently machine-enforced. Production callers pass no seam, so shipped behavior is unchanged. Defect fix plus test seam in existing product code, unrelated to this plan's cohorts; recorded because the file is part of the tracked production bundle and its digest changed since the pre-gate snapshot.

This round closes three further completion gaps the implementation review identified: (1) new documents (and the pre-binding legacy-shape upgrade) now prefer `resolveDefaultTaskBindingV1`'s ownership-derived binding (`workflowRuntimeServicesV1.ts`'s `getVerifiedTaskBindingIdV1`, tagged `taskBindingSource: "ownershipDerived"`) over the bare path/canonicalId `localDigest` stand-in whenever the task folder has genuine, live-validated ownership to derive one from — `appendChatInteraction`'s binding-conflict check now also treats an `ownershipDerived` document as authoritative, matching `coordinatorSupplied`; (2) `readChatInteractions` now also backfills a durable transaction's own `answers` (present from `answersDraft` onward) into a still-`unresolved` mirror record whenever they differ, not only a settlement, so a crash between `doSubmitInteractionAnswers`'s durable-first write and its mirror write (chatView.ts) cannot leave the mirror showing a blank, already-submitted question again; (3) `resetChatHistoryV1` no longer marks a mirror interaction `resetByChatRecovery` when its durable transaction counterpart genuinely FAILS to settle (only a benign `ok`/`missing` outcome counts as settled) — the interaction is left `unresolved` instead, so a later read's reconciliation keeps retrying it rather than the two records permanently disagreeing — and its no-document branch now applies the exact same private-storage-availability gate as the with-document path, rather than silently bypassing it. Evidence refresh 2026-07-27 second pass (closing three further implementation-review completion blockers): (a) `resetChatHistoryV1`'s Reset contract — "every unresolved interaction is cleared" — is now enforced as a whole-operation guarantee: if ANY unresolved interaction's durable settlement fails, the entire Reset now fails (`ok: false`) and leaves chat-v1.json completely untouched (no resetEpoch bump, no interaction changes at all) instead of returning `ok: true` while an interaction remains unresolved; (b) the no-document Reset path no longer skips the write-and-verify-a-snapshot contract — it now provisions the same registered chat-recovery locators and writes/verifies the fresh empty document itself as the snapshot (the true pre-reset state) before committing it as chat-v1.json, exactly like the with-document path; (c) adds `readChatDocumentIdentityV1`, a new exported read of the CURRENT document's own `{documentId, taskBindingId}` — consumed by chatView.ts's `resolveInteractionRef` so Answer/Cancel/Resume can supply a server-derived, non-client-controlled task/document binding for the conversation orchestrator to validate. Reached from the production bundle via chatView.ts (already-tracked). Evidence refresh 2026-07-27 third pass (closing the implementation review's remaining completion blocker: structured posting must always carry the complete coordinator binding): `NewChatDocumentInteractionV1.binding` is now REQUIRED (not optional), and `appendChatInteraction` runtime-validates its presence/shape and rejects a call that omits it — it can no longer silently fall back to a bare path/canonicalId stand-in the way a plain message append still legitimately may. `emptyDocumentFor` was split into two functions: the original (folder-path + canonicalId, `resolveDefaultTaskBindingV1` fallback) now serves ONLY the unrelated Reset-with-no-prior-document path, while the new `emptyDocumentForInteractionV1(binding)` seeds a brand-new document exclusively from a structured-question posting's mandatory coordinator-supplied binding. Evidence refresh 2026-07-27 fourth pass (closing the implementation review's architectural blocker on the consumer side — "Chat self-registers a bare path and synthesizes a localDigest binding when no ownership binding is available"): ALL Chat storage registration now flows through one dispatch point, `ensureConversationChatRootV1` — a TASK conversation's folder goes through workflowRuntimeServicesV1.ts's strict, ownership-backed `ensureWorkflowTaskFolderRootV1` (missing progress, missing ownership, an underivable binding, a dead workspace owner, an uncontained location, or a mismatched caller binding all REFUSE the operation), and ONLY the Global Assistant's reserved conversation identity (`isGlobalAssistantConversationV1`) goes through the separated `ensureWorkflowNonTaskStorageRootV1`. `localTaskBindingId`'s path/canonicalId stand-in is now used EXCLUSIVELY for that one non-task conversation — a task conversation's default binding is ALWAYS the folder's ownership-derived binding (`resolveDefaultTaskBindingV1` reads it back from the strict registration and throws an invariant violation rather than falling back if it is somehow absent), so the review's "localDigest when no ownership binding is available" case can no longer occur for any task. `appendChatInteraction` additionally enforces the exact-binding contract for task conversations: the required coordinator-supplied `binding.taskBindingId` must EQUAL the binding freshly derived from the folder's current persisted ownership (via `ensureWorkflowTaskFolderRootV1(folder, { bindingId })`) before any document read or write — a stale, foreign, or rebound claim fails closed.
